FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A122
At a four-way stop the first to arrive goes first, and only a near tie is settled by yielding to the vehicle on your right. [A122]
Why it matters: group_hint four-way-stop; prereq_hint sec09-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F08.
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A122
A left-turning driver yields to straight and right-turning traffic at a four-way stop, while at a two-way stop any turning driver yields to the one going straight. [A122]
Why it matters: group_hint stop-controlled; prereq_hint sec09-R01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F09, sec09-F10.
Source: [A122 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0122]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A123
Signaling 100 feet ahead is the minimum before a turn across oncoming traffic, and the turn itself must end in the lane nearest your starting side, with lane changes only afterward. [A123]
Why it matters: group_hint turning; prereq_hint sec09-F07; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F11, sec09-F13.
Source: [A123 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A124
U-turns in Washington are allowed by default unless a sign bans them, yet a curve or an approaching hilltop still rules one out because you cannot see in every direction. [A124]
Why it matters: group_hint u-turns; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F15.
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A124
At a T-intersection the through road has priority, and at a Y-intersection the major road has priority, so in both the driver on the ending or minor road waits. [A124]
Why it matters: group_hint intersection-types; prereq_hint sec09-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F17, sec09-F18.
Source: [A124 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A125
A calming circle uses ordinary intersection right-of-way rules and may have no signs at all, and large vehicles there may even circle clockwise. [A125]
Why it matters: group_hint circles; prereq_hint sec09-F07; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F20, sec09-F21.
Source: [A125 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A127
Entering a roundabout you look left and yield to traffic already circling, and once inside you hold your lane until your exit rather than changing lanes. [A127]
Why it matters: group_hint roundabouts; prereq_hint sec09-F22; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F26, sec09-F27.
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A127
In a roundabout, an approaching emergency vehicle means continue through and then pull over, not stop in the circle. [A127]
Why it matters: group_hint roundabouts; prereq_hint sec09-R07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F28.
Source: [A127 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0127]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A129
In a diverging diamond the left turn onto the freeway needs no stop and no yielding to oncoming traffic, because the design removes conflicts with oncoming vehicles, though you still follow the signs and markings. [A129]
Why it matters: group_hint interchanges; prereq_hint sec09-F29; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F30.
Source: [A129 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A129
At an uncontrolled intersection the driver coming from a secondary or unpaved road yields to the one on the state highway or paved road. [A129]
Why it matters: group_hint uncontrolled; prereq_hint sec09-F31; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec09-F32.
Source: [A129 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A121
Stopping at the stop line comes first, and creeping slowly forward is a second step used only when the view of the cross street is still blocked. [A121]
Why it matters: group_hint entering-intersections; prereq_hint sec09-F03; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec09-F04.
Source: [A121 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0121]
